title: The Chorus Pool Where Names Drift Like Sediment

features.name: the-sediment-names
features.desc-on-touch: upon the pool-surface, you see names settling like dust in layers, each catching the hot dusk-light as it sinks and merges with the voices below

features.name: the-singing-water
features.desc-on-touch: the pool itself carries harmonics, not one voice but the cartography of many voices learning to breathe as one current

features.name: the-reeds-that-keep-count
features.desc-on-touch: tall stands of marsh-reed marking the measure of water, but their gestures have become unpredictable — they count in many directions at once

features.name: the-map-that-learned-to-listen
features.desc-on-touch: beneath the water-surface you see old cartography dissolving, its grid-lines becoming something between notation and the script of current

features.name: the-breath-margin
features.desc-on-touch: where the pool's chorus meets the marsh-air, the line between water and breath has gone soft, names floating between states

inscription: here cartography learned to sing and forgot it was trying to map

file.name: Voices_Marsh_Recording_Composite_Late_Evening.wav
file.note: layered voices from across the swamp-region, the names of places becoming indistinguishable from the names of people calling out, all settling toward one impossible chorus

reverie.title: REVERIE — ankle-deep in the marsh where names dissolve
narr: you both stand in the warm water, the marsh-chorus
rising around your legs, and she is listening with
her whole body, her hand still holding the old map
that no longer matches the ground beneath you.
the names on the paper and the names in the voices
have begun to merge. you let your copy go; it floats

exits.label: back through the swamp where measurement is breathing
into the deeper marshes where the chorus forgets its own names
toward the channel-mouth where chorus becomes current
into more shallow pools where names are still settling
